summary: This is a new Housing Bill, not an amendment. Asma Rasheed submitted it on behalf of the government on 22 April 2025. It has 82 articles and would create a "Housing Act". The Ministry would have to write a national housing policy, strategy and survey, and every company or body that runs a housing project would have to register with the Ministry and get a permit for each project. It sets minimum standards that every housing unit must meet, lays out who can get social housing and how flats are given out and taken back, and sets up a Housing Fund. It also creates a complaints, appeal and fines system.
whyItMatters: People buying flats from developers would get legal protections, such as advance payments going into escrow accounts and honest sales brochures. Families without proper housing would have a legal route to social housing: a needs list, published rules and points-based allocation, with ties decided by lottery.
keyProvisions: Articles 7 to 9: the President sets a national housing policy on the Minister's advice, reviewed at least every 5 years. The Ministry must publish a national housing strategy and a housing needs survey within 6 months of the law starting. After that, the survey is repeated every 10 years.

Articles 11 to 18: anyone running a housing project must register with the Ministry and get a permit for each project. Advertising, booking or selling units before the permit is banned. Buyers' payments must go into an escrow account, and projects already under way must register within 180 days.

Articles 19 to 31: every housing unit must have safe water, reliable electricity, waste collection, a sewerage connection and telecom access. It must also have a private toilet, a kitchen, a bedroom and a living area, plus accessibility features, lifts in multi-storey buildings, emergency exits, light, ventilation and firefighting equipment.

Social housing (Chapter 6): applicants must be Maldivians aged 18 or over who lack adequate housing and have low financial means, judged by an income and assets test. The income threshold is set by the Minister, published in the Gazette and reviewed every 3 years using the consumer price index. Priority goes to people with disabilities, carers of dependent parents and victims of domestic violence.

Social housing rules: the Ministry keeps a confidential register of people needing housing, reviewed every 12 months. Units are allocated by points, with ties decided by lottery. Renting out a social housing unit is banned. It can pass only to a spouse or child who also qualifies, and eviction requires 3 to 6 months' notice.

Articles 64 to 82: a Housing Fund must be set up within 90 days, run by a governing board the Minister appoints, and it can give housing loans. The Ministry handles complaints, and people can appeal to a review committee and then to court within 30 days. Fines are up to MVR 50,000, plus MVR 25,000 for each repeat. Regulations are due within 9 months, and the law starts 2 months after it is published in the Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Families without adequate housing, people buying flats from developers, housing developers and agencies, local councils, and the housing Ministry.
statedReasons: The government says the bill sets up a housing system that lets everyone living in the Maldives reach safe, adequate housing and helps those in most need find a place to live. It also sets rules for registering housing providers, running projects responsibly, and the standards that developed housing must meet.
